transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I guess what finally made me come in is that I just keep forgetting basic adult things. Like... paying my bills, returning emails for job interviews, showing up for appointments, or just following through on regular errands. It's getting really frustrating because it's actually starting to cost me real opportunities, so I realized I needed to do something about it.
Did these kinds of forgetfulness or difficulty following through start back in childhood?

Yeah, they definitely did. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright, but... I constantly lost my worksheets. I would rush through directions without really reading them, and I talked out of turn a lot. And my desk was just a complete disaster—it was always so messy that I could never actually find my assignments when it was time to turn them in. So, yeah, it's been happening for a long time.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a longstanding, childhood-onset pattern of inattention and disorganization with current adult functional impairment. Symptoms include losing items, failing to follow through, careless rushing through directions, difficulty organizing tasks/space, and talking out of turn, with documented impact on bills, job applications, appointments, and errands. This is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation.
